scope.summary: This standard specifies comprehensive guidelines, operational practices, and safety protocols for the environmentally sound storage, collection, transport, refurbishing, dismantling, and recycling of electrical and electronic waste (e-waste) to maximize material recovery and prevent ecological contamination.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Quality and Operating Guidelines (Environment and Ecology / Waste Management)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 17862:2026 is an operational and management guideline standard rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its structured storage guidelines, collection channels, and equipment calibration schedules is legally integrated into Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) authorizations. It is universally audited by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) to verify that EEE producers, dismantlers, refurbishers, and recyclers follow environmentally sound practices.

requirements.detail:
Formally defines a 'producer' of electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) under three categories:
a) Manufactures and offers to sell EEE and their components, consumables, parts, or spares under its own brand;
b) Offers to sell under its own brand, assembled EEE and their components, consumables, parts, or spares produced by other manufacturers or suppliers; or
c) Offers to sell imported EEE and their components, consumables, parts, or spares.

Producers of EEE may establish and finance collection channels across all cities, towns, and villages where their products are sold to encourage and facilitate safe disposal of old or unused electronic devices.

Producers must provide clear and accessible details of their established collection networks through appropriate media, including publishing active website links where the general public can easily retrieve this information.

All diagnostic, testing, sorting, dismantling, and material-handling equipment utilized in e-waste processing facilities must be regularly calibrated, monitored, and maintained on a specified periodicity to ensure occupational safety and prevent emissions.
All collection points, warehouses, refurbishing centres, and recycling plants must be established and operated strictly by authorized dismantlers, registered refurbishers, and licensed recyclers.

Collected e-waste, especially components containing hazardous chemicals or heavy metals (such as cathode ray tubes, liquid crystal displays, lithium-ion batteries, and printed circuit boards), must be stored in secure, weatherproof, and climate-controlled areas to prevent rainfall ingress, leachate runoff, or physical damage.

Refurbished electrical and electronic equipment intended for resale must satisfy safety and quality requirements, aligning with the Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17862 : 2026 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard code of practice specifying guidelines for the storage, collection, refurbishing, dismantling, and recycling of electrical and electronic waste (e-waste). Developed under the Waste Management Sectional Committee (EED 08), this first revision replaces the legacy 2022 edition to align with India's latest Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations. It defines strict classifications for EEE producers, requires them to finance and establish nationwide collection channels with clear website disclosures, and enforces operational guidelines for authorized facility operators—mandating climate-controlled storage to prevent heavy metal leaching and regular calibration of dismantling and testing equipment.
